assignments.reason: כבוד ה (the honor/glory of God) is identified in the text as 'בְּחִינַת כְּבוֹד הַתּוֹרָה' — the honor of Torah. The Rebbe explicitly links it to rain via 'וּכְבוֹד ה' נִרְאָה בֶּעָנָן'. Honor/glory of God and Torah is the positive, elevated dimension of revelation — it belongs by essential nature to the domain of malkhut and gadlut (Kingdom and Greatness, Package 2), because malkhut here is the state of elevated spiritual standing from which Torah is revealed with honor. כבוד ה is the manifestation of the gadlut/malkhut state: when Torah is revealed properly from a state of greatness, God's honor is seen. Its polarity is unambiguously good — it is the positive force whose inversion (חלוף הכבוד, Package 1) produces the evil mirror.

The Torah innovations that are revealed (חדושי התורה שמגלין) are the active expression of the gadlut/malkhut state. The Rebbe explains that R' Shimon's revealing of Torah brings R' Akiva into gadlut (Package 2). The revelation of Torah chiddushim IS the function of malkhut/gadlut — one reveals Torah from the state of greatness. This concept is essentially the active face of what Package 2 describes: the elevated state that enables and compels Torah revelation. Note: 'חדושי תורה שמגלין' (edge 3) is the same node with minor spelling variation.

connected_to: ממשיכין אותו, כביכול. ולהיכן נמשך האלקות – לתוך מח השומע
assignments.reason: Torah in this teaching is not an abstract concept but the revealed Torah — the Torah that is spoken from a state of gadlut/malkhut. The text equates Torah revelation with the hasadim from the father (יוחאי אבא = the Torah = חסדים מצד האב), and Torah is the vehicle through which one enters gadlut: 'וּמוֹסֶרְךָ לַמַּלְכוּת = bringing to gadlut.' Torah here is essentially the content of what malkhut/gadlut produces and enables. Its essential nature in this teaching is inseparable from the kingdom-and-greatness domain.

The revealing of hasadim (חסדים) is what Torah revelation produces. The Rebbe states: 'הִתְגַּלּוּת הַתּוֹרָה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַחֲסָדִים' — the revelation of Torah IS the revelation of hasadim. This is closely identified with the hasadim from the father (חסדים מצד האב), which is the source enabling gadlut/malkhut. The revealing of hasadim belongs by essential nature to the domain of greatness and positive spiritual abundance — Package 2. It is the outflowing generosity that characterizes the malkhut/gadlut state.

new_packages.proposed_label_en: Rain and the Forces of Nature

nodes.reason: Rain (גשמים) is the central natural phenomenon in this Torah's argument. The Rebbe uses rain as the pivot between the spiritual (כבוד ה bringing rain) and the physical (אדים producing rain / wars stopping rain). Rain itself is a neutral natural force — it can serve the good (falling in its proper time brings blessing) or the evil (being withheld due to חלוף הכבוד, or falling at harvest time as a curse). Its essential nature is a natural mechanism, not inherently aligned with holiness or evil.

The cloud (ענן) is the natural medium through which כבוד ה appears and through which rain comes. The text states 'וּכְבוֹד ה' נִרְאָה בֶּעָנָן, וְעַל־יְדֵי הֶעָנָן בָּא גְּשָׁמִים.' The cloud is a neutral natural vessel — it is the medium, not the spiritual force itself. It belongs with גשמים as part of the natural-phenomena cluster.

The vapors rising from the earth (אדים) are the physical source material of rain. The text explains that rain is made from these vapors, and when there is bloodshed, the vapors are diverted to produce war instead. The אדים are a neutral natural force — they can become rain (good) or become the vehicle of bloodshed (evil, via the wordplay אֵידָם = אֵדִים). Their essential nature is a raw material of nature, serving either direction.

The cessation of armies and wars (נפסקים הגיסות והמלחמות) is the outcome of rain falling. The Talmudic dictum 'בשעת גשמים אפילו גייסות פוסקות בו' places this as a natural consequence of rain. While the cessation of war is a positive outcome, the concept itself describes a state of the physical world — the stopping of military activity as a natural consequence. It is part of the rain/nature cluster because the Torah presents it as the physical correlate of rainfall, not as an intrinsically spiritual state.

new_packages.rationale: These four nodes — rain, cloud, vapors, and cessation of wars — form a natural-phenomena cluster that serves as the physical stage on which the Torah's spiritual argument plays out. Rain is produced by vapors, manifested through clouds, and results in cessation of wars. None of these are intrinsically holy or evil — they are neutral natural forces and states that can be directed by spiritual causes (כבוד ה → rain via the good path; חלוף הכבוד → drought via the evil path). The Torah uses these natural mechanisms as the visible expression of the spiritual dynamics between Packages 1-3. Polarity is neutral because rain, clouds, and vapors serve both the good and evil dimensions of the teaching.
